notes.n10.si: Crowded and consolidating: Accenture leads; Indian majors (TCS reported ~$1.8B annualised AI revenue in FY26) are buying AI and engineering firms (Indian IT spent ~$4.5B on acquisitions in H1 2026).
notes.n10.consult: Strategy firms are shifting to outcome-linked fees and AI-agent leverage, and are co-investing in lab-backed services firms (Bain, McKinsey and Capgemini invested in OpenAI's Deployment Company).
notes.n10.native: Fastest-moving segment in 2026: labs went downstream (OpenAI Deployment Company, $4B+, May 2026; Ode with Anthropic, Jul 2026) and SIs bought boutiques (Accenture-Faculty, Jan 2026).
notes.n10.bpo: Incumbent CX/BPM outsourcers are repricing around AI agents while AI-native outsourcers (Crescendo) and SI-BPO combinations (Capgemini-WNS, $3.3B, Oct 2025) compete on outcome pricing.
notes.n10.skill: Platform consolidation (Coursera-Udemy, May 2026) alongside free vendor academies from labs and hyperscalers that double as ecosystem lock-in.
notes.n10.change: ISO/IEC 42001 certification is becoming the baseline (BSI, Schellman accredited), and AI-specific insurance (AIUC, Armilla, Munich Re) is emerging as a new assurance layer.
notes.n10.lab: Created in 2026: OpenAI Deployment Company (OpenAI-controlled, >$4B, May 2026) and Ode with Anthropic (Anthropic minority, launched Jul 2026), both growing by acquiring boutiques (Tomoro, Fractional AI, Casper Studios).
notes.n10.org: Led by HR consultancies (Mercer, Korn Ferry, WTW, Aon) and the strategy firms; the work is role and work redesign rather than technology build.
notes.n10.managed: SIs and BPOs are repackaging application and process outsourcing as ongoing agent operations, often priced on outcomes.
notes.n10.insure: Early market: specialist MGAs (Armilla, Testudo, AIUC) on Lloyd's or reinsurer capacity, with Munich Re's aiSure the longest-running cover.
notes.n10.partner: Lab and hyperscaler partner programmes now steer services demand; Anthropic committed $100M to its Claude Partner Network in 2026.
